To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current model of university education is not preparing students for the world of work.

The University and the Knowledge Economy (UKE) model of university education, based on a curriculum of knowledge acquisition, a pedagogy of knowledge transfer, and a structural model of education that is based around the academic subject and the academic year, is not well adapted to the requirements of the contemporary labour market, which requires a more holistic approach to education, and a curriculum that includes the development of skills, capabilities and attributes, as well as knowledge.
The University and the Knowledge Economy: The Knowledge Economy and the University in the 21st Century (2014) Edited by: John Holford, David J. Atkinson and John Z. Aytac.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a model of university-based education that will enable students to develop the capabilities that will equip them to be lifelong learners and to adapt successfully to a changing labour market.
developing a more nuanced and sophisticated approach to graduate employability, and the ways that this might be achieved through a more flexible and adaptive curriculum.
the question: How can universities better prepare their students for a world of work that requires flexibility and adaptability?

universities do not prepare their students well enough for the world of work, and that they are not equipped with the capabilities that are required for twenty-first century employment.
the university is not well placed to develop the capabilities that graduates need to be employable.
university-based higher education is not fit for purpose in the twenty-first century.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current higher education model is inadequate for developing the skills, capabilities, and attributes that are required by the contemporary labour market.
